story.headline: England end Spain's 43-match unbeaten run
story.summary: England won 3-2 in Madrid, handing the reigning world champions their first defeat in regulation time since March 2024 and ending a run of 43 matches without a loss (the 2025 Nations League final defe
story.display_body: England won 3-2 in Madrid, handing the reigning world champions their first defeat in regulation time since March 2024 and ending a run of 43 matches without a loss (the 2025 Nations League final defeat to Portugal went to penalties and officially counts as a draw). Harry Kane scored a penalty on 45 minutes, Ezri Konsa and Ben White made it 3-0 by the 57th, and England then hung on after Elliot Anderson was sent off for a foul on Lamine Yamal, which also gave Spain a penalty. Spain pulled it back to 3-2 but a stand-in goalkeeper, James Trafford, made several saves late on.
story.why: A team that had won the Euros and the World Cup without losing was beaten by a side that played the last half hour or so with ten men, which is a useful marker of how even the top of European football has become.

story.headline: Belgium knock Italy out of the quarter-finals
story.summary: Italy entered the last round as group leader after beating France 3-1 on Thursday, but lost 4-1 in Brussels and finished behind both Belgium and France
story.display_body: Italy entered the last round as group leader after beating France 3-1 on Thursday, but lost 4-1 in Brussels and finished behind both Belgium and France. Pio Esposito put Italy ahead on 12 minutes; Maxim De Cuyper and Nathan Ngoy turned it around within seven minutes and Jeremy Doku's solo goal made it 3-1 by the 26th minute. Belgium and France (2-1 winners over Turkey, helped by an own goal) both advance to the knockout quarter-finals. Italy's late penalty miss capped a day on which a first-place position was lost in 90 minutes.
story.why: The group table flipped on the final day: a win over France earlier in the week counted for nothing once Belgium and France both won.

story.headline: Meillard third in Levi slalom
story.summary: Loic Meillard (Switzerland) climbed from eighth after the first run to third, 0.73 seconds behind winner Lucas Pinheiro Braathen of Brazil and 0.17 behind Clement Noel of France
story.display_body: Loic Meillard (Switzerland) climbed from eighth after the first run to third, 0.73 seconds behind winner Lucas Pinheiro Braathen of Brazil and 0.17 behind Clement Noel of France. It was Meillard's 39th World Cup podium and his second of the young season after second place in the Soelden giant slalom. Meillard said the previous days were hard after what SRF calls a shock diagnosis for his sister Melanie, a fellow racer, and that he skied for her. Tanguy Nef was 12th and Daniel Yule 16th. Pinheiro Braathen repeated his 2025 Levi win, which SRF notes no one had managed in 14 earlier Levi slaloms, and has now won a giant slalom and a slalom this winter.
story.why: Switzerland's slalom group has its top technician on the podium at the start of the season, though the 0.73-second gap shows he is still chasing Pinheiro Braathen.

story.headline: Genoni plays 1,000th National League game
story.summary: Zug's Leonardo Genoni played his 1,000th league game in a 4-2 win at the ZSC Lions, joining 19 skaters but no other goalie at that mark
story.display_body: Zug's Leonardo Genoni played his 1,000th league game in a 4-2 win at the ZSC Lions, joining 19 skaters but no other goalie at that mark. A planned celebration on Wednesday 2026-11-11 against Ambri was abandoned after fewer than ten minutes because of holes in the roof, and Genoni sat out the next game. At 39 he has 619 wins, 89 shutouts and seven titles, and has extended his contract with Zug to 2030. The next active goalie, Reto Berra, has 629 games.

story.headline: Andreeva wins WTA Finals
story.summary: Mirra Andreeva won the season-ending WTA Finals, which ran from 8 to 15 November, in a week BBC Sport calls stunning
story.display_body: Mirra Andreeva won the season-ending WTA Finals, which ran from 8 to 15 November, in a week BBC Sport calls stunning. Defending champion Elena Rybakina had withdrawn with a viral illness on 7 November, so the field changed before play began. The match report would not open, so no score or opponent is given here. On the men's side, BBC Sport reports Alexander Zverev's first win as world number one at the ATP Finals in Turin, which began on 15 November.
story.why: The year-end championship is the last big title of the season and decides who carries momentum into January.

story.headline: Racing Bulls keep Lawson for 2027
story.summary: Racing Bulls (Red Bull's junior team) confirmed that Liam Lawson keeps his seat for 2027 alongside rookie Arvid Lindblad
story.display_body: Racing Bulls (Red Bull's junior team) confirmed that Liam Lawson keeps his seat for 2027 alongside rookie Arvid Lindblad. This puts to rest weeks of talk that 19-year-old Bulgarian Formula 2 driver Roman Tsolov would replace Lawson; Tsolov was given a reserve driver role instead. Lawson has 89 points to Lindblad's 38 this season and the team sits fifth in the constructors' standings, which Autosport says will be its best-ever finish.

story.headline: Estonia to shut Russia border crossings
story.summary: Estonia will close its road border crossings with Russia on 1 December after a GRU-attributed arson attempt on drone maker Threod Systems.
story.display_body: Estonia will close its road border crossings with Russia on Tuesday 1 December, its foreign ministry said on Sunday 15 November. The move follows an attempted arson attack on a drone maker near Tallinn that Estonia's Internal Security Service (KAPO) attributes to Russia's military intelligence service, the GRU. Eight Latvian citizens were detained after trying to break into the premises of Threod Systems in Viimsi on Saturday morning, 14 November, with the aim of causing an explosion and a fire, according to the public broadcaster ERR. Threod makes long-range reconnaissance and attack drones. This is the second attempted arson attack on an Estonian defence firm since August, when Milrem Robotics was targeted. Prime Minister Kristen Michal called it "part of Russia's broader hybrid war against Europe", and Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said closing the crossings would also make it harder to get around sanctions. The three crossings affected, Narva, Luhamaa and Koidula, are among the last land routes into Russia still open to travellers from the EU. Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said that, if confirmed, the plan would be "unbridled Russophobia". The attribution to the GRU comes from Estonian authorities and has not been independently verified.
story.why: an EU and NATO state is shutting a land border in response to sabotage against its arms industry. It is the clearest step yet by a Baltic state from naming Russia's hybrid attacks to imposing a concrete cost for them.

story.headline: Prague's biggest protest since 1989
story.summary: Hundreds of thousands rallied in Prague against a bill scrapping the licence fee for Czech public broadcasters.
story.display_body: Hundreds of thousands of people rallied in Prague's Letná park on Sunday 15 November against the government's plan to scrap the licence fee that funds Czech public television and radio. Organisers put the crowd at 400,000, and police, while giving no figure, said it was the largest demonstration since the fall of communism in 1989. The bill, which passed its first reading on Saturday 24 October, would replace the fee with money from the state budget and cut public broadcasters' budgets by 15 to 20%, according to Le Monde. Critics, including the European Broadcasting Union, the European Federation of Journalists and Reporters Without Borders, say it would put Czech Television and Czech Radio under the control of the government. Prime Minister Andrej Babiš, whose ANO party governs with the SPD and the Motorists, says his government does not want to control the public media and that "none of what the people are protesting against… is true". The protest was organised by the Million Moments for Democracy group.
story.why: moving public broadcasters from a dedicated fee onto the yearly state budget makes their funding a decision for whichever government is in office. That is the mechanism media-freedom groups warn about, and the size of the protest shows how contested it is.

story.headline: Third US carrier reaches Middle East
story.summary: The USS Theodore Roosevelt arrived in the CENTCOM area, joining two other US carriers as US-Iran talks stall.
story.display_body: The aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt has arrived in the Middle East, a US official told Al Jazeera on Monday 16 November. It is the third US carrier now in the area run by US Central Command (CENTCOM). The deployment comes as talks to turn the US–Iran truce into a lasting settlement and to reopen the Strait of Hormuz remain stalled. Pakistan and Qatar are mediating. Last week, President Donald Trump said further strikes on Iran were "quite unlikely" and the military part of the war "effectively over", while saying US forces remained "locked and loaded". The Revolutionary Guards claimed drone attacks on a US site in Bahrain on Friday 13 and Sunday 15 November. The Roosevelt left San Diego in September, so its arrival had been expected.
story.why: Trump has called the war "effectively over", but a third carrier adds strike capacity and points the other way, and the president's own statements have not been a reliable guide to what happens next.

story.headline: ICC judges close US Afghanistan probe
story.summary: ICC judges closed the investigation into alleged torture by US forces in Afghanistan and CIA sites, citing evidentiary limits and delay.
story.display_body: Three judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) closed its investigation into alleged crimes by US forces in Afghanistan on Thursday 12 November, Le Monde reported on Monday 16 November. The investigation, opened in 2020, covered torture, rape and sexual violence at the US base at Bagram, north of Kabul, in 2003 and 2004. It also covered CIA secret prisons in Romania, Poland and Lithuania. According to Le Monde, the judges cited "significant limits" on the prosecution's ability to investigate and gather evidence, and said it was now too late to bring charges. Lawyers for former detainees at the US Center for Constitutional Rights had argued that the evidence of a torture policy, including the US Senate's own report, was overwhelming. Le Monde says Washington had made closing the case one of its conditions for not sanctioning the Court ahead of April 2027.
story.why: this was one of the few avenues for international accountability for US abuses after 9/11. It is closing at a moment when the US is pressuring the Court. The judges, for their part, gave procedural reasons: the time that has passed and the limits on gathering evidence.

story.headline: Neves re-elected in Cape Verde
story.summary: José Maria Neves won re-election with 63.8% in the first round, per provisional results.
story.display_body: Cape Verde's President José Maria Neves won a second five-year term in the first round on Sunday 15 November, with 63.8% of the vote according to the electoral commission's provisional results. His main challenger, former justice minister Joana Rosa Amado of the Movement for Democracy (MpD), took about 31.6%. Four other candidates shared the rest. Le Temps, citing AFP, says turnout was low. Neves promised to keep "promoting freedoms" in the archipelago, which ranks third in Africa on the Mo Ibrahim Foundation's 2026 governance index. Observers from ECOWAS (the West African regional bloc), the African Union and the EU monitored the vote.

story.headline: Swiss economy grows 0.2% in third quarter
story.summary: Seco's first estimate puts Q3 2026 Swiss GDP growth at 0.2%, led by industry with services flat.
story.display_body: Switzerland's real GDP grew 0.2% in the third quarter of 2026, according to the first estimate from the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (Seco), published on Monday 16 November. Industry grew again while services as a whole stagnated, the wire agency ATS reports. The growth is well below the second quarter, when GDP rose 1.5%, according to the same report. Economists polled by the financial news agency AWP had expected anywhere from −0.3% to +0.4%, so the result is in the middle of that range. The full Seco release, with the breakdown by sector and the figure adjusted for major sporting events, was not reachable this run.
story.why: if services, the larger part of the economy, are flat while industry carries growth, the slowdown is broad. That feeds into cantonal budget forecasts and the Swiss National Bank's next rate decision.

story.headline: Swiss asylum requests fall 16%
story.summary: SEM registered 2,210 asylum applications in October 2026, 16% fewer than a year earlier.
story.display_body: Switzerland registered 2,210 asylum applications in October 2026, 16% fewer than in October 2025 (433 fewer), the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) said on Monday 16 November. Afghanistan remained the main country of origin with 498 applications, followed by Eritrea (430), Algeria (236), Ethiopia (171) and Somalia (163). Applications rose by 88 (4%) from September, which the SEM says is the usual late-summer and autumn rise before winter. The SEM decided 2,419 cases at first instance and granted asylum to 567 people. A total of 732 people left Switzerland under official supervision: 418 on their own and 314 under police escort, either to their home country, to the EU state responsible under the Dublin rules, or to another country.
